open_points.subject: store.read_records missing-identity mode
open_points.text: “The call also names what a missing identity means” conflicts with the operation Inputs, which say only “One record type and identities, or one relation of the closed set”.
open_points.question: How is the missing-identity outcome supplied to store.read_records, and is it one mode for the whole identity read or a separate mode for each identity?
options: One closed enum argument for the whole identity read
A missing-outcome value attached to each identity
Separate read operations for unknown_reference, internal_error and omission
open_points.default_guess: Use one closed enum argument for the whole identity read.

open_points.subject: selection of omission for store.read_records
open_points.text: “omitted from the answer, unknown_reference (an identity the caller's own caller named), or internal_error (an identity a stored record names, which the store must hold)” gives provenance rules for two outcomes but none for omission.
open_points.question: Which reads must name omission, especially computed-identity existence probes and optional lookups, and must every caller contract state that choice explicitly?
options: Use omission for computed identities and optional existence probes
Permit omission wherever a module chooses it
Do not use omission in State 5 callers
open_points.default_guess: Use omission only for computed-identity existence probes and explicitly optional lookups; use unknown_reference for request-supplied identities and internal_error for identities referenced by stored records.

open_points.subject: omitted identity result handling
open_points.text: “one that names omission answers the records found” conflicts with “a caller never checks the answer for absence itself”.
open_points.question: How can a caller use an omission-mode identity read to decide that a record is absent: may it branch on the shortened result, or must store return a tagged found/not-found result that does not require comparing the answer with the request?
options: Caller may branch on an omitted or shortened result
Store returns a tagged result for every requested identity
Omission is allowed only for display reads whose caller never needs to distinguish missing identities
open_points.default_guess: Return a tagged result per requested identity for omission-mode reads.

open_points.subject: sandbox.execute_function result when a parent limit cannot be set
open_points.text: “then no environment was created and the execution is crashed” while Outputs still require “resources used”.
open_points.question: What resources_used does sandbox.execute_function return when the parent cannot set a limit before bubblewrap starts and no sandbox environment is created?
options: A present record containing measurable setup consumption
No resources_used for this crashed outcome
open_points.default_guess: Return a present zero-valued resources-used record.

open_points.subject: FlowConstant composition input
open_points.text: “value: the value_id of a StoredValue … written when the version is composed” while flows.compose_flow_version takes only “constants with declared classes” and A01 refuses caller-supplied value identities.
open_points.question: What exact constant representation enters flows.compose_flow_version so it can validate and write the StoredValue: does the caller provide literal canonical value bytes plus declared schema and class, or some other non-value_id structure?
options: Target port, literal value, declared schema and declared class
Target port and an existing value_id
Target port, literal value and class, deriving the schema from the target port
open_points.default_guess: Accept the target port, literal value, declared schema and declared class; compute and persist the value_id inside composition.
